questions.q: Which catalog view shows Query Store's current storage size against its configured maximum?
options: sys.database_query_store_options
sys.dm_os_wait_stats
sys.query_store_runtime_stats
sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations
questions.explain: sys.database_query_store_options exposes actual_state_desc, current_storage_size_mb, max_storage_size_mb, and readonly_reason.

questions.q: What happens when Query Store hits its size cap with SIZE_BASED_CLEANUP_MODE = OFF?
options: Query Store flips to read-only — it keeps serving historical data but silently stops capturing anything new
SQL Server automatically shuts down the database
Query Store immediately deletes all its data
Nothing changes; capture continues indefinitely regardless of the cap
questions.explain: With cleanup mode off, hitting the cap sends Query Store into READ_ONLY — historical data stays queryable but nothing new is captured, often without anyone noticing right away.

questions.q: What does SIZE_BASED_CLEANUP_MODE = AUTO do differently from OFF?
options: It proactively removes the oldest, least useful data to stay under the cap, so Query Store keeps capturing continuously
It disables Query Store entirely once the cap is reached
It doubles the max storage size automatically
It has no effect on cleanup behavior
questions.explain: AUTO is the recommended default specifically because it avoids the silent read-only failure mode that SIZE_BASED_CLEANUP_MODE = OFF can produce.

questions.q: What column tells you specifically why Query Store went read-only?
options: readonly_reason on sys.database_query_store_options
wait_type on sys.dm_os_wait_stats
last_force_failure_reason_desc on sys.query_store_plan
state on sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations
questions.explain: readonly_reason on sys.database_query_store_options explains why Query Store flipped to read-only, such as hitting the size cap.

questions.q: According to this lesson's production checklist, what should QUERY_CAPTURE_MODE be set to on most busy production databases, and why?
options: AUTO, to skip low-value ad hoc queries and reduce capture overhead unless there's a specific reason to capture everything
ALL, always, regardless of workload
NONE, to avoid any overhead whatsoever
It doesn't matter and has no effect on overhead
questions.explain: AUTO reduces the write and storage overhead of Query Store by skipping cheap, infrequent ad hoc queries, which is the recommended default for most production systems.
